questions.question: Let $S$ be a feasible set and $f$ an objective function. The problem $\min\,f(\boldsymbol{x})$ over $\boldsymbol{x}\in S$ is equivalent to which maximization problem?
A problem $\min\,f(\boldsymbol{x})$ over a feasible set $S$ is rewritten as $\max\,-f(\boldsymbol{x})$ over $S$. How do the optimal solution vectors of the two problems compare?
options: They are each other's negatives, $\boldsymbol{x}$ and $-\boldsymbol{x}$
They are unrelated and must be found separately
They coincide only when $f$ is nonnegative on $S$
They are exactly the same vectors in both problems

questions.question: A problem $\min\,f(\boldsymbol{x})$ over $S$ has optimal value $z_{\min}$, and $\max\,-f(\boldsymbol{x})$ over $S$ has optimal value $z_{\max}$. How are $z_{\min}$ and $z_{\max}$ related?

An LP $\min\,\boldsymbol{c}^{\top}\boldsymbol{x}$ subject to $\boldsymbol{A}\boldsymbol{x}\ge\boldsymbol{b}$, $\boldsymbol{x}\ge0$ is converted to a maximization problem. What happens to the constraints?
options: They stay exactly as they were, still $\boldsymbol{A}\boldsymbol{x}\ge\boldsymbol{b}$
Their right-hand sides are negated, giving $\boldsymbol{A}\boldsymbol{x}\ge-\boldsymbol{b}$

questions.question: Why is a minimization problem often rewritten as the maximization of the negated objective before it is solved?
options: It makes the optimal objective value positive
It lets a procedure for maximization solve it
It removes some of the constraints of the model
It guarantees that the optimal solution is unique

questions.question: A minimization problem has the objective $4x_1-2x_2+x_3$. Which objective does the equivalent maximization problem use?

The problem $\min\,2x_1-3x_2$ subject to $x_1+x_2\le4$, $x_2\le3$, $x_1,x_2\ge0$ is solved as $\max\,-2x_1+3x_2$ under the same constraints, with optimum $(0,3)$ and value 9. What is the solution of the original problem?
Which maximization problem is equivalent to $\min\,5x_1+4x_2$ subject to $x_1+x_2\ge3$, $x_1\le2$, $x_2\le2$, $x_1,x_2\ge0$?

A firm compares three feasible plans with costs $f(A)=12$, $f(B)=7$ and $f(C)=9$ and wants the cheapest one. It solves $\max\,-f$ over these plans instead. Which plan and value does this problem return?
A cost-minimization LP is solved as the maximization of the negated cost, and the transformed problem has optimal value $-15$. What is the minimum cost?
options: $-15$, the transformed value as it stands
$15$, the transformed value with its sign changed
$15$, but only if all cost coefficients are positive
$-15$, since the costs were negated for the run

questions.question: Why do $\min\,f(\boldsymbol{x})$ and $\max\,-f(\boldsymbol{x})$ over the same feasible set $S$ have the same optimal vectors?
options: Negation reflects the feasible set through the origin
The function $-f$ takes the same values as $f$ on $S$
Negation reverses every comparison of objective values
Both problems always have their optimum at the origin

questions.question: A problem $\min\,f(\boldsymbol{x})$ over a nonempty feasible set $S$ is unbounded: $f$ takes arbitrarily large negative values on $S$. What holds for $\max\,-f(\boldsymbol{x})$ over $S$?
options: It has a finite optimum, as maximizing reverses the problem
It is infeasible, as no vector gives a finite value
It is unbounded below, just as the original problem
It is unbounded, as the negated values grow without limit

questions.question: A modeller converts a minimization problem by negating the objective coefficients of the decision variables, but the objective also contains a constant term: $2x_1+x_2+7$. What must happen to the constant?
options: It must be dropped, as it is not a coefficient
It must be negated as well, giving $-2x_1-x_2-7$
It must stay $+7$, as only coefficients change sign
It must move to the right-hand side of a constraint

questions.question: The problem $\min\,3x_1+2x_2$ subject to $x_1+x_2\ge4$, $x_2\le2$, $x_1,x_2\ge0$ is solved as $\max\,-3x_1-2x_2$ under the same constraints. What are the optimal values of the transformed and of the original problem, in that order?

For $\min\,2x_1+x_2+7$ subject to $x_1+x_2\ge12$, $x_1,x_2\ge0$, a modeller solves $\max\,-2x_1-x_2$, dropping the constant, and reports minus its optimal value as the minimum. What is reported, and what is the true minimum?

The problem $\min\,x_1+x_2$ subject to $x_1+2x_2\ge4$, $3x_1+x_2\ge6$, $x_1,x_2\ge0$ has its optimum at $(1.6,1.2)$. A modeller negates the objective and also both constraints, getting $-x_1-2x_2\ge4$ and $-3x_1-x_2\ge6$. What does the modified model give?
options: An unbounded problem, as the constraints now point the other way
An infeasible problem, with no feasible point at all

questions.question: Which problem over the same feasible set $S$ has exactly the same optimal vectors as $\min\,f(\boldsymbol{x})$ for every function $f$?
A solver only accepts minimization problems. To find $\max\,g(\boldsymbol{x})$ over $S$, an analyst solves $\min\,-g(\boldsymbol{x})$ over $S$. How are the results related?

The problem $\min\,3x_1-5x_2$ subject to $x_1+x_2\le4$, $-x_1+x_2\le2$, $x_1,x_2\ge0$ is solved as the maximization of $-3x_1+5x_2$ under the same constraints. What is the optimal vector, the transformed value and the original optimal value?

For $\min\,3x_1-5x_2$ subject to $x_1+x_2\le4$, $-x_1+x_2\le2$, $x_1,x_2\ge0$, a modeller writes the maximization objective as $3x_1+5x_2$, negating only the coefficient of $x_1$, and reports minus its optimal value as the minimum. What do they report?
